headline: 300 tourists evacuated as fire breaks out at The Sea Princess Hotel in Cox's Bazar
summary: A fire erupted in the generator room of the hotel's ground floor, prompting a swift evacuation. Hotel staff and fire service quickly brought the blaze under control, preventing major casualties.
details: A fire broke out in the generator room of The Sea Princess residential hotel at Sugandha Point in Cox's Bazar on Friday afternoon. Over 300 tourists were staying at the hotel at the time of the incident.

The blaze, believed to have originated from a generator short circuit, started around 4 PM in the ground floor parking area. Quick action by hotel staff and fire service personnel prevented a major disaster.
Hotel employees initially used fire extinguishers to control the fire before a Fire Service unit arrived. The combined efforts brought the fire under control within approximately half an hour.
No casualties or injuries were reported among the tourists or staff. All guests were safely evacuated from their rooms as soon as the news of the fire spread.
The generator in the parking area and several other parts of the hotel sustained damage. The hotel director stated they have a 20-member fire service trained team on site.
This incident follows a tragic fire on October 17 at TupTup Resort in Ukhia's Inani area, which resulted in the deaths of 10 tourists.

headline_marked: [[Bus torched after two killed]] in Chattogram road crash, highway blocked for 90 minutes
headline: Bus torched after two killed in Chattogram road crash, highway blocked for 90 minutes
summary: Two autorickshaw passengers died after their vehicle was rammed by a bus on the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar Highway. Angry locals then set the bus on fire and blocked the road for about 90 minutes.
details: Two autorickshaw passengers were killed on Friday night after their vehicle was rammed by a bus on the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar Highway in Satkania’s Nayakhal. The incident occurred around 8 PM.
Following the fatal crash, angry protesters blocked the road and set the bus on fire. This brought traffic to a complete standstill on the busy highway for approximately an hour and a half.
Dohazari Highway Police Station chief Nurul Absar confirmed that traffic resumed normally around 9:30 PM. Police intervened to remove the protesters from the road and restore order.

Locals reported that a bus, traveling from Satkania’s Keranihat towards Chattogram City, veered out of control. It first rammed a parked motorcycle before colliding with the autorickshaw, severely injuring its passengers.
